mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In any 12-month rolling window, the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.05, or the average 20-day return in periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.25% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals persistent inflationary pressure that may trigger premature monetary tightening, causing a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL (YoY) exceeds 5.0%, the average 20-day SPX return is not negative (mean >= 0) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which signals an imminent economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline, the 60-day SPX return is not negative (mean >= 0) or the interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05 in a regression of SPX returns on the interaction term).

mechanism_narrative: During the early stages of an economic recovery (as indicated by UNRATE below 4.5%), a declining unemployment rate signals strengthening labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.5%, the average 5-day SPX return is not positive (mean < 0) or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor in the early recovery regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 3-month moving average indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In any 12-month rolling window, the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.05, or the average 20-day return when INDPRO is above its 3-month MA is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1.6 million units per month, it signals strong consumer confidence and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1600.0, the average 20-day SPX return is not positive (mean < 0) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), an accelerating rate hike path compresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the average 60-day SPX return is not negative (mean >= 0) or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, the 20-day SPX return is not positive (mean < 0) or the interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05 in a regression).
